Displace survey coordinates to protect respondents

Source: R/displace_coord.R
displace_coord.Rd

Moves every survey location in a random direction by a random distance, following the rule of the Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS): urban locations by up to 2 km, rural ones by up to 5 km, and a random 1% of the rural ones by up to 10 km. Households that share a location move together.

Usage

displace_coord(
  x,
  lat = NULL,
  lon = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  urban = 2000,
  rural = 5000,
  rural_far = 10000,
  share_far = 0.01,
  boundaries = NULL,
  water = NULL,
  min_water_area = 0,
  population = NULL,
  min_people = NULL,
  min_scale = 1,
  max_scale = 3,
  seed = NULL,
  max_tries = 100
)

Arguments

x

A survey from prepare_coord(), or a data frame with coordinates in longitude and latitude (WGS84).

lat, lon

<tidy-select> The coordinate columns; read from x when it comes from prepare_coord().

type

<tidy-select> Optional column saying whether each location is "urban" or "rural" (also "U", "R", TRUE for urban). When not given, every location is treated as rural, the larger displacement.

urban, rural, rural_far

Maximum displacement in metres.

share_far

Share of rural locations displaced by up to rural_far.

boundaries

Optional administrative divisions (SpatVector of polygons) a location must stay inside.

water

Optional water bodies (SpatVector of polygons, such as lakes and reservoirs) a location must not land in.

min_water_area

Smallest water body kept from water, in km2.

population

Optional raster of people per cell (SpatRaster or a path), such as WorldPop counts. Requires min_people.

min_people

Number of people that must live within the limit of each location.

min_scale, max_scale

With population, the smallest and largest limit, as multiples of the DHS limit of each location.

seed

Optional seed, for a displacement that can be repeated. Keep it private.

max_tries

Draws allowed per location to land in its allowed area.

Value

x with displaced coordinates, as a c4e_tbl.

Details

Run it before sharing a file with coordinates, or before any variable is computed from them when the team itself should not hold the true locations. Variables computed afterwards (weather extremes, distances, controls) are then based on the displaced locations: the error this adds is small for smooth climate fields and division averages, and larger for short distances such as to the nearest road.

Where a location may land

Three options restrict or adapt the displacement, alone or together:

  • boundaries: a location stays inside the administrative division it started in, so division-level variables are not affected.

  • water: a location never lands in a water body, where no household lives and where extracted values (temperature over a lake, distance to the shore) would be wrong. This costs no privacy, since nobody lives there anyway. Use min_water_area to keep only large water bodies.

  • population and min_people: the limit of each location becomes the radius within which at least min_people people live (inside its division and outside water, when those are given), between min_scale and max_scale times its DHS limit. Sparse places then move further and dense ones less, so every respondent hides among about the same number of people. With the default min_scale = 1 the DHS limits are a floor, as many data agreements require; a smaller min_scale lets dense places move less than the DHS rule. A location that reaches max_scale holds fewer people than asked, and a warning says how many.

What changes in the table

  • The coordinate columns hold the displaced coordinates.

  • Location identifiers built from coordinates (prepare_coord() with id_rule = "coordinates") are rebuilt from the displaced ones, since the old identifiers would reveal the true locations.

  • The context records the rule, the limits and the options used (not the seed). Labels, the Stata codebook and printed tables then say that the coordinates are displaced, and later tables built from these locations carry the record.

Keep seed private: with the seed, the displacement can be undone.

See also

prepare_coord()

Examples

survey <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
coord <- prepare_coord(survey, lat_var = lat, lon_var = lon, id = hhid)

adm_div <- terra::vect(system.file("extdata", "adm_div.gpkg", package = "c4e"))
displaced <- displace_coord(coord, boundaries = adm_div, seed = 1)
#> No `type` given: every location is displaced as rural (up to 5 km).

# how far each location moved, in km
moved <- terra::distance(as.matrix(coord[c("lon", "lat")]),
                         as.matrix(displaced[c("lon", "lat")]),
                         lonlat = TRUE, pairwise = TRUE) / 1000
summary(moved)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>  0.6269  1.8889  2.8668  2.7001  3.5859  4.9381 
c4e_labels(displaced)
#>                                             lon 
#> "longitude, displaced up to 5/10 km (DHS rule)" 
#>                                             lat 
#>  "latitude, displaced up to 5/10 km (DHS rule)" 

# a lake to avoid, and a radius holding at least 5,000 people
lake <- terra::buffer(terra::vect(cbind(30.6, -0.4), crs = "EPSG:4326"), 8000)
people <- terra::rast(adm_div, resolution = 0.01)
terra::values(people) <- 50 * terra::values(terra::cellSize(people, unit = "km"))
displaced <- displace_coord(coord, boundaries = adm_div, water = lake,
                            population = people, min_people = 5000, seed = 1)
#> No `type` given: every location is displaced as rural (up to 5 km).
#> Finding the radius that holds 5000 people for 12 locations.
